purpose: 128-point end-to-end run, the measurement the 1.65x speedup was for: settle the cold-spectrum question and get an end-to-end number on a grid where HMcode sees a real spectrum
setup: our solver on np.geomspace(1e-3, 5.0, 128), two cosmologies (sum m_nu = 0.06 and 0.30 eV), each compared against CAMB mead2020 on a 16384-point spectrum, wall time 6166 s and 6655 s

correction_to_an_earlier_claim.wrong_claim: the 6.4% seen on the 32-point grid was grid error, and the comparison was compressed against a 6.4% floor
correction_to_an_earlier_claim.why_it_was_wrong: quadrupling the grid to 128 points moves the number by almost nothing - m_nu=0.30 goes 6.42% -> 6.33% (total) and 6.30% -> 6.36% (cold). So the ~6% is a real end-to-end error, not a grid artifact.
correction_to_an_earlier_claim.how_the_confusion_arose: the 1.40% figure it was compared against is HMcode fed CAMB's own spectrum, i.e. HMcode's intrinsic error. The 6.4% here is HMcode fed OUR spectrum. Those are different quantities and the comparison was invalid.
correction_to_an_earlier_claim.status: the corrected statement supersedes the earlier one; treating 6.4% as a grid floor is retired

what_this_establishes.where_it_comes_from: the end-to-end number tracks the linear-spectrum deviation almost one for one, so HMcode's response to its input is close to linear and the LINEAR spectrum is the bottleneck - not HMcode (0.88% on a dense CAMB spectrum) and not grid density
what_this_establishes.consistency_with_the_earlier_breakdown: the earlier 3.50% end-to-end figure decomposed as 0.88pp from HMcode plus ~2.6pp from our linear input; this run says the same thing more starkly, with the linear input carrying essentially all of a 4-6% budget

cold_spectrum_final_verdict.overall: MIXED and small. It helps by 0.35pp at f_nu = 0.0045 and costs 0.03pp at f_nu = 0.022. No improvement can be claimed. Commit 30afb7d stays UNVERIFIED in the sense of 'not shown to help', and the change is small enough that either choice is defensible on this evidence.
cold_spectrum_final_verdict.shape_note: at m_nu = 0.30 the cold spectrum trades a high-k deficit for a low-k excess: k=4 goes 0.9495 -> 0.9679 (better) while k=0.1 goes 1.0091 -> 1.0458 (worse), and the max|dev| location moves from k=5 to k=0.031

caveat_about_this_scripts_linear_column.why_it_cannot_be_read_as_linear_error: the ratio computed is p_cold_ours / CAMB_pk_lin, and CAMB's pk_lin is the TOTAL matter spectrum. So the number mixes our numerical error with the genuine physical difference between the cold and total spectra, which grows with f_nu. It is not a numerical accuracy measure.
caveat_about_this_scripts_linear_column.the_real_linear_number: still the previously measured median +0.17% from delta_m against CAMB's delta_tot

cost: 6166 s and 6655 s for the two cosmologies, 128 k points each, at 1.65x faster than before the optimisation - so this class of experiment costs roughly 1.7 hours with the current solver
